milestone.title: V0.2 Judge & Problem Service
milestone.description: First formal implementation milestone after Phase 0. Deliver the published 0.2.0 judge/problem contracts, real Linux sandbox validation, backend integration and traceable release evidence. Foundation/owner-license decision tracked separately.

issue_id_policy: Pxx IDs are stable work-package references, not chronological order. depends_on is the authoritative DAG; GitHub issue numbers/URLs are populated in docs/architecture/implementation-plan.md after creation.

issues.title: Phase 0: establish and verify the repository engineering foundation
issues.body:
## Outcome

Initialize this long-lived repository before V0.2 business implementation: durable governance, contracts, ownership, reproducible tooling, security/compliance provenance and an actionable implementation backlog.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§1, 8, 9; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§1, 14. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- Durable AGENTS.md, README, contribution/security rules, versioned byte-traceable contracts, accepted ADRs, API/migration/upstream/release policies.
- Pinned upstream bootstrap, portable PostgreSQL/tooling environment, meaningful CI and explicit separate Linux security-validation workflow.
- Inspect GitHub configuration; protect main with a documented emergency administration route, keep dev usable, create milestone/labels/scoped Issues.
- Independent reviews from the nine requested perspectives; reconcile findings, verify commands/configuration/links/provenance, commit and push to dev.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Contract snapshots retain source evidence and no historical contract is silently changed.
- [ ] Actual validation outcomes and remaining Linux/runtime limitations are recorded; no mock result counts as sandbox verification.
- [ ] Initialization changes are pushed to dev; no normal direct main push and no final dev-to-main release PR.
- [ ] Owner project-license decision remains explicit; do not assign a project license without authorization.

## Dependencies

Phase 0 foundation; no implementation Issue prerequisite.

## Outside this Issue

Full JudgeTask, scheduler, problem import/publish or production sandbox implementation is deferred to the milestone Issues.

issues.title: Resolve V0.2 contract clarifications before affected implementation
issues.body:
## Outcome

Resolve the bounded implementation blockers in the [V0.2 contract resolution register](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/open-questions.md) jointly with the named contract/backend/database/security owners. Preserve supplied `0.2.0` documents byte-for-byte; publish explicit approved clarification or successor contracts instead of guessing.

## Questions and affected work

- Q-001: recover the absent whole-system architecture/integration contract and exact revision. Blocks P19/P20 final integrated claims.
- Q-002: agree canonical hashing field scope/ordering/Unicode/numbers/null/array semantics and golden vectors, including path resource identity. Blocks divergent P01/P08/P12/P14/P15 cross-service semantics.
- Q-003: approve per-package license evidence intake/reviewer workflow and retention of unsupported/rejected originals without fictitious validated identities. Blocks P03/P04/P07 publication paths.
- Q-004: agree recovery graph and initial-versus-recovery retry budget boundaries/timestamps/events for judge and imports. Blocks P07/P13 recovery.
- Q-005: reconcile immutable artifacts, validation pointers and evidence-only re-review with artifact uniqueness at unchanged source/adapter. Blocks P02/P03/P04/P06 affected schema, persistence and upgrades.
- Q-006: agree duplicate submission attempt and initial-DRAFT withdrawal rejection codes, replay state/header semantics and pre-accept import 422 versus post-accept asynchronous errors. Blocks affected P07/P08/P12 fixtures.
- Q-007: freeze typed manifest/checksum/conversion/default/checker protocol profile shared by importer/runtime. Blocks divergent P05/P06/P11 execution inputs.
- Q-008: reconcile exact demo gRPC localhost:5051 with contract bottom loopback:5050; review supported transport/binding or provenance-preserving adapter. Blocks P11/P16 wiring. Do not quietly add a listener or change the contract.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Every question records agreed owner answer, evidence, affected Issues, compatibility impact, tests and approved clarification/versioned amendment where required.
- [ ] Cross-service answers are jointly reviewed with backend; schema answers with database; isolation answers with security/deployment.
- [ ] Unresolved items block only the affected behavior; unrelated foundation/fixtures work continues.
- [ ] No resolution edits published contract history, fabricates license rights, loosens sandbox security or crosses service ownership.

## Dependencies

Phase 0 question/evidence register. Each implementation Issue consults applicable Q IDs before finalizing its behavior.

## Outside this Issue

No broad contract rewrite, arbitrary extra endpoint, project-license decision or implementation authorization during Phase 0.

issues.title: Owner decision: choose the Code Startrack project license
issues.body:
## Outcome

The repository owner explicitly selects Code Startrack-owned source licensing after reviewing MIT and Apache-2.0; upstream software and imported problem content keep their own independent license evidence.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§8; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§5, 14. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- Review docs/licenses/project-license-decision.md and pinned upstream LICENSE/NOTICE evidence.
- Record owner selection, copyright holder and year policy, then consistently add project LICENSE, source/package metadata and distribution documentation.
- Retain upstream MIT attribution, Moby/seccomp Apache-2.0 NOTICE obligations and problem-specific license gates regardless of project selection.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Commercial use, modification/redistribution, attribution, Apache NOTICE/patent grant and current dependency compatibility are reviewed.
- [ ] Selection is owner-authored/approved and no SPDX identifier is guessed.
- [ ] Before any production/public distribution: license/NOTICE payloads and dependency/problem inventory are verified in the actual artifact.

## Dependencies

Phase 0 foundation; no implementation Issue prerequisite.

## Outside this Issue

No automatic MIT/Apache selection. A project license never substitutes for problem-package review. Engineering bootstrap may proceed while the owner decision is pending.

issues.title: Resolve problemtools nested VIVA binary provenance before image redistribution
issues.body:
## Outcome

Resolve the nested binary provenance and distribution obligations in pinned Kattis/problemtools before shipping its worker image. Root MIT does not settle every bundled component.

## Evidence

Pinned `v1.20260907` / `6010cbaa37a1612117f49566b2fff8646d53faa2` support/Makefile installs `support/viva/viva.jar`. Its SHA-256 is `6590cf1bcea23e27bc4c0ca86ca365343ee85a19671b42ef9815aaaa451b8aa9`. Pinned debian/copyright declares `support/viva/*` MIT, copyright 2010–2018 David van Brackle. VIVA therefore has an upstream license declaration.

The jar also includes nested `miglayout15-swing.jar` (SHA-256 `79db2dea6c4f024285a648c51be82c333345b82958e14f7fb5f6920f0b455d85`) and Eclipse JDT JarRsrcLoader classes. Phase 0 inspection found no embedded LICENSE/NOTICE for those nested artifacts. Their exact versions, provenance and applicable obligations remain unresolved; do not invent SPDX identifiers or describe VIVA as wholly unlicensed.

See [pinned dependency evidence](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/upstream/dependencies.md) and retained upstream licensing texts.

## Deliverables

- Obtain exact nested source/version/provenance, authoritative license texts/NOTICE and applicable redistribution obligations; update inventory/notices and validate actual image contents.
- Alternatively, propose and review a provenance-recorded minimal-build/omission patch excluding the unresolved binary components while preserving required verifyproblem/default checker and contract validation behavior.
- Record technical compatibility impact, patch content/reason, regression results and upgrade implications. Any upstream patch remains separate from owned adapter code.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Every shipped nested component has verified source/version/license/notice evidence; no attribution guessed from library names.
- [ ] If excluded, actual build/install image inventory proves exclusion and the real pinned package-validation/default-checker regression suite passes.
- [ ] Release/compliance owner approves the chosen route; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, license texts, SBOM/compatibility inventory reflect actual artifact content.
- [ ] P06/P16/P20 cannot claim redistributable production image until this gate is resolved. Fixture/source review may proceed without redistribution.

## Dependencies

Phase 0 pinned upstream evidence; coordinate with P06 validation and P16 image owners. This Issue precedes image redistribution and P20 release acceptance.

## Outside this Issue

No guessed MIT/Apache/EPL classification for nested code, automatic project-license choice, dropping required validation checks or silently omitting binaries in Phase 0.

issues.title: V0.2: bootstrap service configuration and strict internal HTTP contracts
issues.body:
## Outcome

Create the owned judge-problem-service process and reusable internal HTTP/DTO boundary without importing backend business ownership.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§1, 2, 3, 5, 9; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§1. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- Record the business-service language and source-directory ownership/seams in an ADR; select an exact compatible patched toolchain after reviewing both upstream go 1.26.0 directives. Pin native dependencies and lock a reproducible service build without silently changing contractual runtime commits.
- Add documented build/start commands and actual native formatting/lint/unit/contract checks to Make/CI; retain portable mocks while execution is unqualified.
- Entrypoint/configuration with validated DB/private-storage settings, independent BACKEND_JUDGE_TOKEN and JUDGE_BACKEND_TOKEN, redacted errors and graceful lifecycle.
- Reusable strict DTO, envelope/error, requestId, pagination, Id/UUID/UTC and size-limit validation; contract fixtures shared by later handlers.
- GET /health exact raw contract object with dependency capabilities wired conservatively; remain unavailable for unimplemented or failed sandbox capability.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] A fresh developer can reproduce the locked build and run the native checks; exact toolchain/build identity and planned source ownership are documented, with no floating toolchain resolver in release builds.
- [ ] Missing/wrong bearer token is 401; browser Cookie grants no authority; body/header requestId mismatch and unknown fields are rejected.
- [ ] Positive decimal bigint IDs remain strings; UTF-8 bytes, null/required fields, safe counters and ms/bytes are tested with boundary/negative cases.
- [ ] No callback URL/command/test-data inputs are admitted; errors/logs leak no secrets, SQL or stack trace.
- [ ] Health 200 requires DB, private storage and real sandbox self-checks; degraded judge refuses new execution while available historical reads remain possible.

## Dependencies

Phase 0 foundation; no implementation Issue prerequisite.

References identify prerequisite interfaces/artifacts/checkpoints; design and inert fixtures may proceed in parallel. Security/compatibility acceptance gates must pass before affected behavior is enabled. P10 supplies inactive configuration before P17; P17 baseline precedes P06 execution, and P20 repeats against the final image.

## Outside this Issue

No user/RBAC/Submission/CF/analysis/portrait implementation; no fake ready judge or mass endpoint business implementation.

issues.title: V0.2: immutable problem/version/artifact repositories and private storage lifecycle
issues.body:
## Outcome

Implement owned immutable identities and checksum-addressed private objects so accepted history remains reproducible after new imports and releases.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§1, 3, 5, 7; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§2–7, 10, 14. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- Repository models for stable source identity, version numbering, base-version links, source/normalized artifacts, tests and reference programs.
- Private object abstraction with checksum verification, immutable writes, safe path/size/symlink handling and database registration/orphan cleanup.
- Transient judge-source lifecycle: backend remains owner, in-flight copies survive, terminal copies/workdirs purge after 24h without deleting historical package/results.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Same source identity stays one problemId; same pinned source/adapter reuses matching artifact; differing checksums cannot overwrite historical bytes.
- [ ] Version contents/tests/references and published evidence are immutable; metadata-only versions share artifact and retain old content.
- [ ] Crash between object write and DB commit leaves a collectible orphan, never an accepted task/version pointing at missing bytes.
- [ ] Private objects, hidden tests/answers/reference code and raw logs are absent from public DTOs and normal logs; credentials cannot access backend source storage.

## Dependencies

P02

References identify prerequisite interfaces/artifacts/checkpoints; design and inert fixtures may proceed in parallel. Security/compatibility acceptance gates must pass before affected behavior is enabled. P10 supplies inactive configuration before P17; P17 baseline precedes P06 execution, and P20 repeats against the final image.

## Outside this Issue

issues.body:

- Version/artifact-specific immutable evidence and documentation for third-party content review and attribution propagation.

issues.title: V0.2: persistent asynchronous OJ-Lab import jobs
issues.body:
## Outcome

Expose contracted fixed-source imports with durable recovery and independent per-package outcomes; validated imports create DRAFT versions only.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§2, 3, 7, 9; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§8, 14. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- POST/GET problem-imports strict request/DTO handlers with full 40-character revision, fixed repository and 1..100 unique safe problems/ paths.
- Durable lease/fencing import worker with short SKIP LOCKED claims, bounded recovery and no network long transactions.
- Fetch pinned commit in dedicated acquisition stage; execution stage offline; immutable checksum provenance and ordered atomic item updates.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] 202 first accept/200 identical replay, different body 409; concurrent duplicates create one persistent job.
- [ ] SUCCEEDED/PARTIAL/FAILED item/count/error/finishedAt rules are correct; whole-source failure rejects all items; one failure preserves other validated drafts.
- [ ] Restart/lease expiry resumes same job and fenced stale worker cannot commit; new import does not advance catalog or publish.
- [ ] Package/license failures surface through item.errors on GET 200, with hidden paths/content/logs safely private; unsupported/rejected originals follow Q01 decision.

## Dependencies

P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06

References identify prerequisite interfaces/artifacts/checkpoints; design and inert fixtures may proceed in parallel. Security/compatibility acceptance gates must pass before affected behavior is enabled. P10 supplies inactive configuration before P17; P17 baseline precedes P06 execution, and P20 repeats against the final image.

## Outside this Issue

No arbitrary repository/archive URL, automatic publication or backend admin authorization implementation.

issues.title: V0.2: versioned server-controlled language capabilities and toolchains
issues.body:

- Immutable language config versions, at most one active per language, deterministic capabilityVersion and safe /languages DTO.
- Language/problem effective intersection and frozen task limits/template/digest handoff; analysisSupported local policy flag.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Stage 1: cpp17/main.cpp template/toolchain artifacts are provided while inactive. Stage 2: cpp17 becomes available only after P17 baseline actual isolated compile/run verification; Java/Python never appear as planned capabilities.

- [ ] Unavailable runtime yields 503 JUDGE_UNAVAILABLE, no fabricated compiler/digest or active unsafe language.

## Dependencies

P01, P02

issues.title: V0.2: persistent task scheduler, leases and fenced crash recovery
issues.body:
## Outcome

Run accepted tasks durably with bounded resource concurrency and safe recovery from worker/runtime failure.

## Authority

[API contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/api.md), §§5, 9; [Database contract](https://github.com/STAR-Ability/code-startrack-judge/blob/dev/docs/contracts/v0.2/database.md), §§10, 13. Implement the published `0.2.0` contract; record unresolved conflicts in the contract clarification tracker before changing semantics.

## Deliverables

- Short SKIP LOCKED task claim, DISPATCHING before runtime dispatch and RUNNING only after confirmed execution; process-local concurrency is not the queue.
- Lease owner/fencing token, 30s heartbeat/180s expiry, at most 3 recovery executions and fresh per-attempt artifacts.
- Shutdown/maintenance handling and reconciliation of old processes/results; terminal source/workdir cleanup via private-storage lifecycle.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] Restart recovers same taskId/requestId/frozen version; stale/expired owner cannot update status/results/outbox.
- [ ] Heartbeats do not increment revision; every visible change increments; terminal facts never regress; recovery-visible regressions use greater revision as DB contract requires.
- [ ] Exhausted recovery becomes FAILED/IE+JUDGE_INTERRUPTED; ordinary TLE is completed user verdict, not infrastructure retry/new submission.
- [ ] Kill/race/disconnect tests demonstrate exactly one committed terminal result and bounded concurrency protects colocated services.
- [ ] No in-flight source cleanup or cross-attempt file reuse; cancellation is maintenance-only and obeys result/error/finishedAt contract.

## Dependencies

P11, P12, P14

References identify prerequisite interfaces/artifacts/checkpoints; design and inert fixtures may proceed in parallel. Security/compatibility acceptance gates must pass before affected behavior is enabled.
